title: Lulu and Velvet's Lost Pillow
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a little room painted the colour of sunshine and filled with soft cuddly toys, lived a duck named Lulu. Lulu was a very fluffy duck. Her feathers were as soft and white as a brand-new cloud, and she adored napping. She would find the softest, coziest spot, give a little wiggle of her tail feathers, and drift right off to dreamland.

Every day, in that same cozy room, but just outside the window, lived a special friend of Lulu’s. This friend was a bat, but not just any bat. This was Velvet. Velvet had wings as soft and smooth as the finest dark velvet. He did not much fancy napping in the bright sunshine. He preferred to hang upside down from his favourite leafy branch, where he could watch the world with his big gentle curious eyes. Lulu would find the softest spot for a snooze, and Velvet would hang from his branch, enjoying the peaceful quiet and the gentle sway of the leaves.

Until one day, something quite unexpected and very lovely happened. A tiny fluffy feather pillow, lighter than a dandelion puff and softer than a whisper, floated in through the slightly open window. It bobbed and swayed like a little boat on a calm sea, and it landed softly on Lulu’s favourite fuzzy rug. Velvet, from his leafy perch outside, saw it too. He tilted his head, his big eyes blinking. This little pillow looked a little sad, as if it had lost its way. It seemed to be waiting for someone, but nobody was there to claim it.

Because they wanted to help, Lulu, with a soft gentle “Quack?”, waddled over to the pillow. She nudged it with her beak, feeling its incredible softness. It was just as soft as her own favourite napping spot. Velvet, with a silent flutter of his velvety wings, glided down from his branch and hovered near the window.

“It seems to have lost its way home,” he whispered, his voice as quiet as the rustle of autumn leaves.

Lulu nodded her fluffy head. With a shared glance they decided they must help this little pillow find its owner.

Because of that, Lulu and Velvet began to look around the sunlit room. Lulu peeked under the little bed, where the dust bunnies usually hid, hoping the pillow had not tumbled there. Velvet, with his sharp kind eyes, looked behind the flowery curtains, which often held forgotten toys and stray ribbons. But the little pillow just bobbed gently, swaying with every tiny breeze that whispered in from the open window. Lulu gave a small concerned quack, her fluffy tail giving a little worried twitch.

Because of that, the little pillow drifted, ever so slowly, towards the window sill. It was almost ready to float right out into the big dusky evening that was just beginning to peek through the sky, painting it with soft purples and oranges. They knew if it floated away, it might never find its home again. Lulu’s fluffy tail twitched again, a little faster this time.

Until finally, Lulu had a most wonderful gentle idea. “Let’s be very, very careful,” she quacked softly.

Velvet understood perfectly. With utmost care, they very, very gently nudged the pillow, guiding it away from the tempting window sill and towards the little bed where a small girl was just beginning to stir from her own nap. Her eyes blinked open, wide and sleepy, and there, right beside her, nestled amongst her blankets, was her lost fluffy pillow. A big joyous smile spread across her face, chasing away any lingering sleepiness. She reached out with her little arms and hugged it tight, burying her nose in its soft fluff. The pillow smelled faintly of lavender, and she could feel the tiny embroidered star on its corner.

Lulu and Velvet watched from their quiet spot, their hearts feeling as warm and full as the midday sunbeam on Lulu’s favourite napping spot.

And ever since then, Lulu the fluffy duck and Velvet the gentle bat kept a watchful eye by the sunshine wall and the leafy branch, ready to help any little thing that seemed lost find its way back home, safe and sound.
